newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Congress undecided on PM's ex-party chief.
newsitem.headline: India's Congress undecided on PM's ex-party chief.

text.p: India's Congress party said on Thursday it was still making up its mind whether to support a state leader whose fate could determine the future of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's coalition.

Gujral is facing pressure from colleagues in his Janata Dal (JD) party and leftist allies in his 15-party United Front (UF) to kick out a breakaway JD group, the Rashtriya (national) Janata Dal (RJD) headed by low-caste chief Laloo Prasad Yadav.
Yadav, who is fighting allegations of corruption, is also resisting moves to oust him as Chief Minister of the eastern state of Bihar.
"The high command is yet to take a decision (on supporting Yadav)," Congress spokesman Vithal Gadgil told Reuters. "The situation is so fluid, nothing can be said with certainty."
Yadav is seen needing the Congress party's support to survive in office with his band of his breakaway legislators.
Congress, which is not a member of the UF, has reiterated its vital support to Gujral's minority government in the federal parliament.

If the Congress helps to topple Yadav in an expected confidence vote in Bihar, Gujral would be saved the embarassment of having to choose between Yadav and the leftists, who politicians say may otherwise consider quitting the coalition.
The leftists want Yadav to quit his chair in Bihar because he is facing federal police charges in a $280-million corruption scandal linked to alleged embezzlement of animal welfare funds.
Yadav, who denies any wrongdoing, has resisted calls to quit and face trial.
Last Saturday, Yadav, who was president of Gujral's Janata Dal, formed a breakaway group, the RJD, alleging voter lists were rigged in a party presidential election he lost on Thursday.
Yadav immediately pledged to continue to support Gujral's coalition, saying he had nothing against the prime minister.
Gujral has so far resisted pressures to act and seek the removal of RJD from the minority coalition. He has also resisted calls to sack three ministers from the RJD, which was formed last Saturday.
